NutriFresh Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Foods's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Growth Officer; and Maria Gonzalez, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: E-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, Impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, EBITDA margin performance and key factors, Performance of key brands and product categories, and Key achievements and challenges in the quarter.

First, regarding E-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: Our e-commerce channel continues to demonstrate remarkable agility in the evolving Food & Beverage landscape, positioning us firmly toward an omnichannel model. In the third quarter, e-commerce sales hit $433 million, reflecting a solid 48% increase from the prior year and a 12% rise sequentially from Q2. This extends our streak to 11 straight quarters of double-digit growth in this area. E-commerce now makes up 15.2% of our total net revenue of $2.85 billion, a significant jump from 8.4% a year ago and just 4.7% in Q3 2020. Over that period since the start of the pandemic, we've achieved a compound annual growth rate exceeding 75% here, surpassing the overall F&B e-commerce market's 32% CAGR as tracked by Nielsen.

This penetration level aligns us with top players like Mondelez at about 14% digital sales and ahead of Kellogg's at 12%. Our premium stance in functional beverages and plant-based snacks gives us an edge, with online orders averaging $45 compared to the $32 industry benchmark from IRI, unlike more basic categories such as soft drinks where Coca-Cola sees around 10% from e-commerce.

Breaking it down by region, North America dominates, accounting for 62% or $268 million of our Q3 e-commerce sales and growing 52% year-over-year. This stems from strong ties with Amazon Fresh, Instacart, and Walmart+, where our NutriThrive Energy Drinks and NutriBar protein snacks lead in health and wellness rankings. E-commerce penetration in North America reached 18% of regional sales, mirroring the U.S. online grocery surge to 13% overall per Brick Meets Click, especially as suburban millennials buy shelf-stable functional items amid rising inflation.

Europe contributed 24% or $104 million, up 42% year-over-year, via our direct-to-consumer site and links with Ocado and Carrefour online. EU Green Deal regulations have spurred interest in our organic kombucha offerings, pushing e-commerce to 12% of European revenue. In APAC, 10% or $43 million grew 65% year-over-year, spearheaded by China on Tmall and JD.com, where urban growth and middle-class expansion echo U.S. patterns—e-grocery at 15% in Chinese cities according to Kantar. Emerging markets in LATAM added 4%, with initial successes on Mercado Libre for our ready-to-drink nut milks.

Driving this are targeted investments addressing F&B logistics hurdles like perishability and cold chain needs. Our NutriFresh Direct platform, powered by Shopify Plus and Klaviyo CRM, now engages 2.8 million active users and uses Dynamic Yield's AI for personalized recommendations, such as our Immunity Boost Pack pairing snacks with vitamin waters, lifting average order value by 28%. Subscription options, similar to Chobani's model, now represent 22% of DTC repeat business for items like shelf-stable yogurt pouches.

On marketplaces, enhanced Amazon A+ content and FBA tweaks boosted core SKU velocity by 15%, while Instacart back-to-school promotions for kid-friendly functionals increased share of wallet. We've cut returns 18% to below 3% with improved recyclable, leak-proof packaging, and Gopuff collaborations for quick commerce in 10 cities now make up 8% of e-commerce sales.

Beyond growth, e-commerce boosts margins at 42.5% gross versus 38% in brick-and-mortar, due to direct sales capturing full $18.50 average consumer value over $12.50 wholesale and avoiding slotting fees. This added 150 basis points to our overall gross margin this quarter. We're aiming for 20% e-commerce share by fiscal 2025, adding AR features for beverage trials and Roblox metaverse events for Gen Z. In a tough environment with 7% grocery inflation and private label gains, online builds loyalty—our Net Promoter Score reached 68 digitally versus 55 offline.

Second, concerning Impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: These persistent issues, intensified by geopolitics, weather extremes, and post-pandemic fragilities, have squeezed our cost of goods sold and margins across our snacks, beverages, dairy, and plant-based lines. Year-over-year, key input costs climbed 18% in Q3, above the 12% sector norm seen by PepsiCo and Mondelez. Agricultural staples led: wheat up 22% from Russia-Ukraine tensions and U.S. Midwest droughts affecting cracker and pretzel production; corn rose 15% impacting high-fructose corn syrup in our NutriFizz beverages; sugar eased to 10% post-Brazil harvest but cocoa jumped 45% for chocolate snacks, akin to Hershey's concerns.

Proteins and dairy faced avian flu driving poultry 25% higher for meals and nuggets, with skim milk powder up 16% from New Zealand's El Niño-hit exports. Packaging saw aluminum for cans rise 12% on European energy volatility and PET resin 20% from Asian disruptions; manufacturing labor added 8-10%, averaging 6.5% wage hikes in North America.

These factors trimmed consolidated gross margins 210 basis points to 32.4% from 34.5% last year; core compression was 150 basis points post one-offs, hitting snacks and beverages hardest at 60% of the impact, contributing to 4% lower adjusted EBITDA at $532 million despite offsets via pricing and mix.

Supply disruptions extended lead times 25% quarter-over-quarter to 56 days average. Red Sea issues hit 15% of Asia-Europe spice and palm oil routes by 3-4 weeks, similar to Unilever and Nestlé reports. Gulf hurricanes stalled corn millers, spiking costs 30%; Indian monsoons cut rice 10% for ethnic foods. U.S. West Coast strikes cost $5 million extra in freight, European trucking up 18% on diesel.

Impacts differed by region: North America (55% revenue) saw 20% inflation from energy/labor, moderate disruptions but 12% poultry stockouts shifted to plant-based like our BeyondNutri patties up 15%. EMEA (25%) worst at 25% inflation from energy/Ukraine, but wheat hedging covered 80%; 5% dairy export deferral. APAC/LATAM (20%) milder at 12%, aided by local Thai palm oil, though China port delays hit beverage launches 20 days.

Mitigations delivered results: hedged 75% of 2024 commodities (up from 60%), saving $120 million; secured 50% 2025 wheat/corn 10-15% below futures via CME and Cargill. Diversified suppliers 30%, shifting 40% dairy to U.S./Mexico, JVs for Indonesian palm oil cutting volatility 25%. AI forecasting with SAP IBP/IBM Watson raised turns to 10.2x, stockouts down 40%; IBM Food Trust blockchain on 70% chain saved $8 million yearly; Bayer precision ag improved crop efficiency 12%.

Pricing captured 65% inflation—8% on snacks, 6% beverages—keeping volumes flat; premium/private label mix upped ASP 5%; cut 150 low-margin SKUs for 50 bps gain. Sustainability sourcing at 40% Rainforest certified mitigates risks, adds 3% ASP on cocoa. $200 million robotics target 300 bps expansion by 2026.

We see inflation easing to 8-10% Q4, 5-7% 2025 per USDA/FAO; lead times to 50 days; 100-150 bps Q4 margin recovery, full-year EBITDA $1.85-1.90 billion high end.

Third, in terms of EBITDA margin performance and key factors: Our EBITDA margin reached 18.7% this quarter, expanding 150 basis points year-over-year from 17.2% and 40 basis points from Q2's 18.3%. This is our best in five years, ahead of full-year midpoint 18.0-18.5%, with trailing twelve-month at 18.4%—beating industry ~16% like Mondelez/Hershey, thanks to operational leverage.

Revenue grew 7% organically to $2.85 billion on 4% volume, 3% pricing. Beverages (AquaSparkle waters, iced teas) at 55% mix expanded to 22.1% from 20.5%; snacks/confectionery (NutriCrunch bars, premium chocolates) to 15.2% from 14.1%, with 12% premium plant-based/low-sugar growth fitting health trends.

Gross margins rose 220 basis points to 38.4%. Hedged 85% 2024 cocoa at $6,200/MT vs. $10,000 spike; reformulated 15% chocolate with shea/illipe. Freight up 5% offset by Maersk/rail, cutting ocean times 12%.

SG&A fell 70 basis points to 13.2% via SAP S/4HANA in 70% plants saving $45 million, AI forecasting down DSO 15 days; Smart Factory IoT/robotics up throughput 11%, wages at 4%. Marketing 60% digital/TikTok/Amazon lifted ROI 25%, 30% beverage velocity.

North America (55%) hit 20.1% on Costco/Sam's 15% multipacks, Clean Label on 80% SKUs. EMEA to 17.8% despite euro FX, Polish energy drink JV up 18%. APAC 19.5% on China seltzers 40%, Indonesia palm pass-through. LatAm 16.4% countered Argentina/Brazil via local sugarcane.

Margin First includes $250 million dairy divestment into UK yogurt buy for 25%+ ROIC; regen ag with Côte d'Ivoire farmers cuts volatility 15%, EU compliant. Q4 guide 19.0-19.5%, FY24 18.3-18.6%; risks avian flu 50 bps, unemployment.

Fourth, looking at Performance of key brands and product categories: Our portfolio across beverages, snacks, and health & wellness showed resilience, with segment net revenues up 6.8% reported, 5.2% organic—2.1% volume, 1.9% pricing, 1.2% premium mix. Eleventh straight organic growth quarter, topping NielsenIQ's 3.4% global F&B average.

Beverages (52%) grew 7.2% organic. FizzFresh Cola (vs. Coke/Pepsi) up 4.1%, flat volume offset by 3.8% pricing, 0.5% zero-sugar mix; FizzFresh Zero +12% volume, 1.2 points U.S. share per IRI amid sugar regs. AquaPure electrolyte water +9.5%, 6% volume, e-comm to 18%; VoltEnergy (vs. Monster/Red Bull) +15.2%, 11% volume on zero/low-carb, now 22% beverage mix in $50B market at 8% CAGR Euromonitor.

Snacks (28%) +4.9% organic. CrunchMax Chips (vs. Lay's) +3.7%, 1.5% volume, 2.2% pricing, 0.8 points NA share Circana on Bold Flavors. NutriBites baked +18%, 14% volume to whole-grain.

Health & Wellness (20%) +12.4%. GreenSip Oat Milk +22%, 16% volume, 85% ACV; BrewBoost RTD coffee +19% cold/nitro; PowerBar Pro protein +14% on gym/work trends.

North America (55%) 6.1% organic, 110 bps share NIQ, 25% e-com. EMEA (25%) 4.2%, pricing/sustainability on 70% FizzFresh recyclable. APAC (15%) 9.8%, China Volt 12%, India hydration 15% to 40k kiranas. LatAm (5%) 7% despite FX.

Premiumization at 42% mix +400 bps, $250M R&D AI flavors/fermentation; S&OP digital twin -30% stockouts, 95% responsible sourcing, 65% consumer resonance Kantar. Q4 trends continue, health double-digit.

Finally, reviewing Key achievements and challenges in the quarter: With functional beverages like Quench+ electrolytes, NutriCrunch bars, PlantPure oat milks, and ready meals, we executed well amid inflation and preference shifts.

Achievements: Revenues $2.85 billion, +9% reported, 7% organic—4% volume, 3% pricing. Beverages (45%) +6% volume, Quench+ zero-sugar +2.2 share vs. Gatorade; snacks +5%, NutriCrunch 15% millennial penetration DTC. North America 11% on low/no-sugar 65%; APAC 14%, India 5k kiranas Quench+ 12% share, PlantPure +22%.

Operations: $280 million gross expansion to 38.2% +150 bps via Supply Chain Resilience 2.0—SAP IBP inventory to 45 days, 85% 2025 hedge; 25% recycled PET Quench+, NPS 72. E-com +28% to 18%, bundling +12% AOV. SKU rationalization 15% low-velocity, $50M A&P to digital; $450M BioFerment tuck-in for gut-health crisps +50 bps FY25 EPS.

Challenges: Dairy +18%, oils +12% El Niño palm; Europe +2% organic from PFAS/sugar regs -3% CSD volume, private label/7% inflation. FX -2 pts Brazil/Argentina; Red Sea +5-7 days freight 15%; Kellogg competition -1 pt savory share; U.S. labor +9%.

Vitality Portfolio 80% innovation to functionals/alt-proteins; $1.2B capex automation/regen-ag. FY24 guide organic 6-7%, op profit +100 bps to 14.5%.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jennifer Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jennifer Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 7% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.4%, impacted by input cost inflation but bolstered by hedging and efficiencies. Operating income was $532 million, and earnings per share were $1.45. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for organic growth of 6-8% and EBITDA margin of 18-19%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, John. As detailed earlier, input costs rose 18% year-over-year, driven by commodities like wheat, cocoa, and dairy, but our hedging covered 75-85% of exposure, saving over $120 million, alongside pricing pass-through and supplier shifts that limited margin compression to 150 basis points core.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Davis (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for new zero-sugar energy drinks and what is the expected contribution to revenue growth?

Raj Singh (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Emily. Our new zero-sugar VoltEnergy variants are rolling out across North America and APAC, building on 15% category growth with targeted digital marketing and e-commerce bundles. We expect them to contribute 2-3 points to organic revenue growth next year through volume gains in health-focused channels.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Maria Gonzalez (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Mike, we're tackling this head-on with diversification—reducing single-source reliance by 30%, nearshoring dairy and palm, and tech like AI forecasting and blockchain for 70% visibility, cutting stockouts 40% and lead times toward 50 days by year-end.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please proceed.

Lisa Wong (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jennifer Lee (CFO):
Thanks, Lisa. We anticipate Q4 inflation moderation to 8-10%, margin expansion of 100-150 basis points via efficiencies and pricing, with full-year delivery at the high end of our organic growth and EBITDA guidance, supported by premium mix and e-commerce momentum.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Thompson for closing remarks.

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriFresh Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
